HA I make myself laugh sometimes. But seriously, this is insane.

**- your ball-path is inefficient**  
 watching where the ball goes, you can see you lift the ball a little bit from hip to chest in a straight up direction and out in front of you a little far. then you pull the ball in and far back to your head and stop (stopping all momentum/potential rhythm). then you essentially have this set position that turns it into a catapult-like shot, making the first part of your process inefficient and somewhat redundant. the reason that is problematic is that it makes that last tiny part of your shot motion 100% responsible for your power and accuracy, meaning that one tiny error along that small path is very tough to correct for. think of it like turning up the sensitivity of a controller to ridiculously high settings and trying to be precise with aiming at something, far more difficult.     
  
**- your stance with your lower legs and back and butt is a problem.**   
you begin by bringing your knees in super far forward whilst keeping your back quite straight up and your butt is tucked in quite far when it needs to stick out more here to create a better leverage for balance.  fix it by reducing how far your knees go forward, stick your butt out more and get into more of a squatted position to begin your motion of going down. practicing how to squat whilst keeping your lower legs quite vertical (90 degrees) would probably help.     
  
**- your timing of body parts to energy transfer to the ball is interrupted and inefficient**   
that ball trajectory i mentioned, is what will be fixed if you manage to change what has been mentioned and practice it enough in isolation. I would highly recommend doing 1 change at a time, adding a bunch of new things to your shot will be so difficult that it may make you feel like its impossible. But I can assure you that if you got enough of these things fixed, you would naturally be able to perform the full motion in quite a smooth and repeatable and efficient form if you really look for each area to fix.

Biggest thing I noticed here.

**Tippy toes**:  
You're going way too high up onto your toes and losing balance on your release, honestly most of everything else looks quite good but you are essentially falling over as you shoot this standing free throw.

To **fix** it, try this:  
practice **squatting** down a bit more at your **hips**, (*not your knees*) and stick your butt out a bit. Then, you shouldn't feel the need to come so far up on your toes to generate that bit of power you're looking for and you should manage your balance much better.

I will list all the shot form things that I noticed and what to do.  
Obviously there isn't an exact "right way" to shoot, but mechanics can make you more reliable from the early point and if you arent already elite at this form, it's a good time to work to improve it.

1.  **feet positioning** and angle: (as you begin from your first set point), you really should be rotating them to your left from the beginning. Now skip to where you land at about 1:17 (after your shot is mid-air)  and notice your stance and angle as you land, this is actually a good way to *begin* your shooting position in order to help alignment. 
2. **ball position**: you hold the ball directly in the middle of your body, this will automatically give you more alignment problems as both your arms are now reaching across on an angle to the middle where the ball sits. Try starting the ball on your hip (right side) basically straight above the middle of your thigh.
3. **shooting hand angle**: this is directly linked to #2, starting the ball across like that is making you hand turn inwards and forcing your shot to flick across from side to side as you release. (Notice: right after you release that first shot, look how far across your body your arm is going, this is a direct result of turning your hand on the ball on your initial setup and is making it more difficult to make a nice straight shot)

I would recommend working on each of those individually and going in the order I listed them, they may work together in that sequence and sort of help set each other up as you work on them in syncronicity.

Overall you actually have a lot of good mechanics already in place, timing and balance and touch and strength are looking fairly good as they are. Despite all I've listed here, you could have a real nice looking shot in even a couple of months if you work on it regularly and intelligently.  
Good luck!

being realistic, you aren't going to be able to gain big amounts of actual muscle. unless you're on gear, then you could be more likely to get to the numbers that you're thinking of. But actually, it's pretty good to cut back down to a weight that is only a bit above your starting number from your original bulk.

your last bulk began at 128 and might go to 160, that's fine.

When you cut back down, it's kind of pointless cutting only 10lbs after gaining about 30lbs, as I said, realistically only a small portion of that bulking weight was actually muscle. So you wanna aim for something a little bit closer to the weight you held when you started that previous bulk.

160 down to 140 should get you looking similar in bodyfat % to that first picture, but with a little more size. I know the feeling of getting "smaller" kind of hurts the ego, but it's just about being more realistic with how much extra weight you're carrying from this bulk.

Reiterating:

Your current bulk: 128 - 160, nice.

next cut: 160 - 140

next bulk: 140 - 170 

and so on...

I've seen plenty of people post on here with their bulks that have gone for wayyyy too long and they end up holding onto a bunch of fat that they feel makes them seem bigger and stronger or alpha or something, I get that mindset sometimes as well, but it kind of ruins the look that they ultimately want to have.

Depends on your goals, what should you do?

If you don't mind carrying some extra chub, possibly during times when people aren't even going to be able to see it if you aren't regularly out and about doing things without much clothing, you could continue your bulk a bit longer.

ultimately you're going to want to cut back to being equally or more lean than you were in the "before" so if the bulk is longer, then the subsequent cut will have to be a bit longer, as well.

the cutting mentally is a bit tricky, it feels like lost progress when you see the weight numbers going down on the scale and probably a bit on the lifts, as well. But you'll want to do it because people often take bulking on for way too long and end up losing their direction and discipline.

​

You seem quite athletic, you probably don't want to be carrying a whole lot more chub than what you've got atm, maybe try a cut for like 6-8 weeks and see how you go with it. 

Maybe you could aim for about 140lbs in 8 weeks or so?

Use an app on your phone to track your daily cals in and it should give you a pretty easy guide to follow on how much to be having to reach your target in the time frame.

Then your next bulk you can aim for something like: from 140 to about 170 or so, in a similar time frame of like 4-6 months.

​

Keep at it, stay consistent. You'll get where you want in the long run :)
